title: $\mathrm{Cons}(X,\Lambda)$ is essentially small
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, and let $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ be defined
in a fixed universe. Then the isomorphism classes of objects of $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ form a set.
Here $\ell$ is a prime, $E$ is a finite subextension of a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and the coefficient rings are the condensed rings of [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back as $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. In particular these are not the discrete constant coefficient sheaves. The full category $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ is that of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Sets and small site skeletons are taken in the larger universe $\mathcal V$ of [def-weil-size-convention], with the schemes and coefficient data in its fixed smaller bound $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$.

proof.text: Apply [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] to the commutative ring object $\Lambda_X$. Its forward equivalence retains underlying abelian sheaves, section groups and restriction maps, so we may use the sectionwise module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] throughout. Its size hypothesis holds on the chosen $\mathcal V$-small site [def-weil-size-convention]; the required monoidal abelian sheafification is supplied by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. In particular we retain the actual pulled-back coefficient ring, rather than replacing it by a discrete constant ring.

source.place: First paragraph, choice of an adapted finite stratification; second paragraph, set of finite stratifications

proof.text: In the bounded universe convention [def-weil-size-convention], the schemes and morphisms under consideration form a $\mathcal V$-set: spaces, rings, sheaf operations and structure maps are data in the set $\mathcal U$. Finite lists of such data over the fixed $X$ form a set. Select the lists of locally closed immersions with disjoint constructible images covering $X$; these are the finite stratifications of [def-constructible-stratification]. Thus the finite stratifications used below form a set. An isomorphic replacement of a stratum within the fixed bound does not affect its image or any sheaf restricted to it.

source.place: First paragraph, choice of an adapted finite stratification; second paragraph, set of finite stratifications

proof.text: The scalar ring $R=\Lambda(*)$ is $E$ or $\Qlb$ by [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]: a map from one point is an element, and every algebraic element lies in a finite subextension. Let $P$ be a finitely presented scalar module. Its presentation [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module] gives finitely many spanning vectors. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free] choose a basis $B$ of $P$. Each spanning vector has finite support in $B$; their union $B_0$ is finite. Every vector lies in the span of $B_0$, so independence forces $B=B_0$. Enumerating $B$ gives $P\cong R^r$ for some $r\geq0$, including $P=0$.

source.place: Tag 09FN, lemma-vector-space-is-free; finite spanning-set support argument

proof.text: The Noetherian scheme $X$ is quasi-compact by the statement's convention and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Hence [sk-def-sfb-constructible](2) supplies a finite adapted stratification $a:S_a\to X$ whose restrictions have the models $\Lambda_U\otimes_R P$ of clause (1). For the basis in step 3, sheafifying the coordinate maps identifies the constant $P$ with the free constant $R$-module of rank $r$; this follows directly from the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-free-scalar-extension] to the constant ring sheaf $R_U\to\Lambda_U$ to obtain $\Lambda_U\otimes_R P\cong\Lambda_U^r$. Its hypotheses allow arbitrary sheaves of commutative rings and finite rank, not just integral lattices. Consequently each $a^*F$ is lisse (pro-étale locally finite free). Clause (2) of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] preserves this on refinements. We now bound the lisse restrictions and the gluing between strata.

source.place: First paragraph, choice of an adapted finite stratification; second paragraph, set of finite stratifications

proof.text: We first identify inverse image along a site object with slice restriction, including for the present nonconstant coefficient rings. If $u:U\to S$ is an object of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$, clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $S_{\mathrm{proét}}/U$. For an object $T\to U$, an index $(V,T\to U\times_S V)$ in the inverse-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is equivalently an $S$-map $T\to V$. The index $(T,\mathrm{id}_T)$ is initial in this category, hence terminal in the opposite indexing category of that formula. The presheaf inverse image at $T$ is consequently $M(T)$, with the original restriction maps. This is already a sheaf because coverings in the slice are the original coverings, so sheafification does nothing. The same calculation applies to the coefficient ring and its action. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], $u^*$ on coefficient modules is this inverse image and $u^{-1}\Lambda_S\simeq\Lambda_U$. Therefore a trivialization $u^*L\simeq\Lambda_U^r$ identifies $L(T)$ with $\Lambda_S(T)^r$ naturally for every $T\to U$.

source.place: Section 00XZ (localization), inverse-image formula; site identification uses more-morphisms.tex Tags 094T/0951 through the cited localization node

proof.text: Fix a stratum $S$ and a lisse $L$. On the chosen small skeleton choose a trivializing covering $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ and integers $r_i\geq0$. Remove repetitions of the same site object, choosing one trivialization for each remaining object; repetitions do not affect the covering condition in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Thus $I$ can be a subset of the set of site objects. There is no need to make the covering finite. On $U_{ij}=U_i\times_SU_j$, the two trivializations differ by mutually inverse matrices $g_{ij}$ and $g_{ij}^{-1}$, of sizes $r_j\times r_i$ and $r_i\times r_j$, with entries in $\Lambda_S(U_{ij})$. Write $g_{ij}$ in the direction from the $i$-coordinates to the $j$-coordinates. On $U_i\times_SU_j\times_SU_k$ the cocycle equation is $p_{jk}^*g_{jk}\,p_{ij}^*g_{ij}=p_{ik}^*g_{ik}$. On the diagonal $\delta_i:U_i\to U_i\times_SU_i$ it is $\delta_i^*g_{ii}=I_{r_i}$. No equation $g_{ii}=I$ on the entire self-overlap is imposed: the two projections of a non-monomorphic cover can give different trivializations there. Indeed a module-sheaf map between finite free modules is determined by the images of its standard basis sections; naturality and linearity give the same matrix on every test object [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Different ranks are allowed, including empty overlaps. All these codes form a set: take subsets $I$ of the fixed object set, functions $I\to\mathbf N$, and products of the matrix-entry sets over pairs of indices, then impose the equations by separation. All coefficient section sets and index sets lie in $\mathcal V$.

source.place: First paragraph, transition data; arbitrary small covers in place of the unnecessary finite quasi-compact refinement

proof.text: A code gives an explicit model rather than requiring a choice from a class of sheaves. For $V\in S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ put $L_c(V)$ equal to the families $s_i\in\Lambda_S(V\times_SU_i)^{r_i}$ such that $s_j=g_{ij}s_i$ on $V\times_SU_i\times_SU_j$, with restrictions componentwise and the $\Lambda_S(V)$-action induced by restriction. This is a sheaf: along any covering of $V$, each component glues uniquely by the coefficient sheaf axiom, and each matrix equality holds after gluing because it holds on that covering. This is exactly the equalizer sheaf condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], applied componentwise; base change of coverings is part of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. If $L$ produces the code $c$, the isomorphisms of step 5 and the sheaf axiom for the covering $\{V\times_SU_i\to V\}$ identify $L(V)$ with $L_c(V)$: a section gives its compatible tuple, and conversely the tuple glues to a unique section. These identifications respect restrictions, addition and scalar multiplication [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Hence $L\simeq L_c$, and the set of codes provides a set of actual sheaves containing an isomorphic copy of every lisse restriction. For an empty stratum the same equalizer is the zero module sheaf.

source.place: Tags 00VM/00VR, definition-sheaf-sets/definition-sheaf; direct equalizer construction, also the gluing-of-maps argument of Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps

proof.text: Fix a finite stratification and one model $L_a$ on each $S_a$. Put $H=\prod_a a_*L_a$, a fixed $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf. This finite product is computed sectionwise: componentwise gluing verifies the sheaf axiom, with componentwise ring action. The functors and adjunctions $a^*\dashv a_*$ exist for these condensed coefficients by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Given $F$ and isomorphisms $\alpha_a:a^*F\simeq L_a$, let $t:F\to H$ have components $a_*\alpha_a\circ\eta_a(F)$. We claim $t$ is monic. Let $k:K\to F$ be its kernel, which is sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The equation $t_a k=0$ implies $\eta_a(F)k=0$, since $a_*\alpha_a$ is invertible. Apply the exact functor $a^*$ of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] and compose with the adjunction counit. The triangle identity $\varepsilon_{a,a^*F}\circ a^*\eta_a(F)=1_{a^*F}$ gives $a^*k=0$. Exactness also makes $a^*k$ monic, so $a^*K=0$ for every stratum. Clause (3) of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] detects exactness on the strata; applied to $0\to K\to0$, it gives $K=0$. Thus $F$ is isomorphic to a subsheaf of $H$. This argument does not require strata to factor through one another or any chosen reduced complement.

source.place: First paragraph, additional gluing between strata: explicit encoding by a subsheaf of the product of the stratum pushforwards, using exact stratum detection

proof.text: For each fixed $H$, its subsheaves form a set. A monomorphism $N\to H$ is injective on sections because kernels are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; identify $N$ with its sectionwise images. Such a subsheaf is determined by the family of subsets $N(V)\subseteq H(V)$, one for each object of the fixed small site, since its operations and restrictions are inherited from $H$. These families lie in the set $\prod_V\mathcal P(H(V))$; imposing module, restriction, and sheaf conditions selects a subset. Therefore subsheaves of $H$ supply a set of representatives containing, up to isomorphism, all the $F$ of step 8. Finally take the union over the set of finite stratifications from step 2 and, for each, over the finite products of sets of codes from steps 6--7. This is a set in $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention] containing a representative of every constructible sheaf. Retain the representatives that are constructible and quotient this set by isomorphism; the result is precisely the asserted set of isomorphism classes. Rank zero and empty strata cause no exception; when $X$ is empty, the empty-stratum detection of step 8 gives $F=0$.

source.place: Second paragraph, set of all data and isomorphism classes; explicit power-set bound for the additional gluing data

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs; descent reconstructed by the sheaf equalizer, with gluing between strata encoded by subsheaves rather than an unproved Ext-size assertion
